messages.content: I need to compare flights for Nashville and Memphis, October 18 through 20. The Nashville meeting starts Monday at 9:30 a.m., and the Memphis inspection is Tuesday at 1:30 p.m. I can either fly round-trip to Nashville or come home from Memphis.

I’ll compare a Sunday flight to Nashville with an early Monday arrival, then price both the Nashville round trip and an open-jaw return from Memphis. About what time will the Memphis inspection finish?
Allow two hours, so 3:30. I’ll have a rental car either way.

The drive from central Nashville to the Memphis location is about 3 hours 15 minutes without a long stop. Returning the car and clearing security add roughly an hour, so driving back to Nashville after the inspection would put you at BNA around 7:45 p.m. at best. Flying from Memphis gives you considerably more margin.
Show me the actual schedules and totals. I don’t want to create a problem for the Monday meeting just to save a little.

For ORD-BNA, the viable Sunday nonstop leaves at 6:20 p.m. and arrives at 7:55 p.m. The lowest workable Monday nonstop leaves at 6:05 a.m. and arrives at 7:36 a.m., giving you 1 hour 54 minutes before the meeting if the flight is on time.

Using the Sunday outbound, the Nashville round trip is $318 with a Tuesday 9:35-11:12 p.m. BNA-ORD return. The open-jaw itinerary is $417 with a Tuesday 6:05-7:49 p.m. MEM-ORD nonstop, or $451 with an 8:15-9:59 p.m. nonstop. All amounts are standard economy totals.
And if I take the Monday morning flight instead?

The Monday-outbound versions are $274 round-trip through Nashville, $373 with the 6:05 p.m. Memphis return, and $407 with the 8:15 p.m. Memphis return. That saves $44 in every structure, but a modest delay Monday would leave little time to get from BNA to the 9:30 meeting.
The Nashville round trip looks cheap, but is that Tuesday return honestly workable after Memphis?

It is possible only with a tight sequence: finish at 3:30, leave Memphis immediately, reach the Nashville airport area around 6:45, return the car, and check in for the 9:35 flight. Ordinary traffic still leaves a buffer, but an inspection overrun or congestion on I-40 could consume it. You would also spend more than six hours driving Tuesday between Nashville and Memphis and back.
No. Compare the two Memphis returns more closely.

The 6:05 p.m. flight requires leaving the restaurant around 3:45. The airport is about 20 minutes away, so you should reach the rental return near 4:05 and the terminal around 4:25. That leaves roughly 1 hour 40 minutes before departure. The 8:15 p.m. flight adds $34 and about two hours of waiting, but it absorbs a substantial inspection overrun and still gets you to Chicago before 10:00 p.m.
The inspection should end on time. Use the Sunday 6:20 flight and the 6:05 out of Memphis. The extra night is worth protecting Monday, and I’d rather be home before eight Tuesday.

That is the $417 open-jaw schedule: ORD-BNA Sunday 6:20-7:55 p.m., then MEM-ORD Tuesday 6:05-7:49 p.m. It supports the Monday 9:30 meeting, allows the Nashville-to-Memphis drive before Tuesday’s 1:30 inspection, and gives about 1 hour 40 minutes at MEM after a 3:30 finish. Would you like me to hold that flight structure for the hotel and rental-car comparison, or ticket it now?
Hold it for the complete-trip pricing. For my seat, make it a window whenever seat selection opens. Carry the later Memphis flight as the fallback, too.

I’ll carry forward the preferred $417 open-jaw schedule and the $451 Memphis-return fallback. No flight has been ticketed. The next comparison will include a Sunday-night Nashville hotel, a rental car picked up at BNA and returned at MEM, the roughly 3-hour-15-minute Nashville-to-Memphis drive, and lodging positioned for Tuesday’s 1:30 p.m. inspection. For the preferred flights, I’ll select or request a window seat for you when seat selection is available; if it is deferred until check-in, that will remain pending until the earliest selection window.
